The line is whole as it stands, and is stored as printed. The section prints no other hazard code. Beside some of the classes it prints precautionary statements, with codes that begin with P: those are not hazard statements and are not carried into the record.

Read and not carried. Section 11, its second line: that the salt may be able to harm an unborn child. The line carries no hazard class and no code. Why: the same sheet does not bear it out: its classification in section 2 has no class for harm to the unborn child or to fertility. Neither of the other two suppliers' sheets has one, the third's says that it has no data on it, and NOAA's record says nothing of it. The note is held to a length and has the classes that the documents do give. It is put here for whoever decides what the note says.

Read and not carried. Section 11, its first line. Section 2 has the irritation, of the skin and of the eyes, and no class for an allergy. Why: the note has the skin allergy from the second supplier's sheet for a solution, which gives it a class and a code; this line agrees with it and has neither.

Read and not carried. The heading of section 4. Under it, for the eyes: they are rinsed with water for several minutes, contact lenses are taken out if they are worn and come out easily, and the rinsing is kept up after that; the sheet gives no number of minutes. Its first line is that anyone exposed or worried gets medical advice (P308+P313). For the eyes it adds medical advice if the irritation lasts. For the skin: it is rinsed with water for several minutes. For swallowing: the mouth is rinsed, and a poison centre or a doctor is called by anyone who feels unwell. Why: it is the first aid of the solid; the note gives the first aid of the second supplier's sheet for a solution, which asks more for the eyes.

supports.prints: H317: May cause an allergic skin reaction.
supports.where: Section 2, the second of the two hazard statements; the class is sensitisation of the skin, category 1A. The first is H303, that the solution may be harmful if swallowed (acute toxicity by mouth, category 5), which is milder than the H302 on the tile. Neither of the first supplier's sheets has a class for an allergy. The note gives this one with its code and says that the solution may set off a skin allergy.

supports.prints: P302+P352: IF ON SKIN: Wash with plenty of water and soap.
supports.where: Section 2, among the precautionary statements. With it are P362+P364, that clothing the solution has got on is taken off and washed before it is worn again; P333+P313, medical attention if the skin is irritated or a rash comes; P272, that such clothing does not leave the workplace; P261, on not breathing its mist; P280, on gloves, protective clothing and protection for the eyes and the face; and P312, a call to a poison centre or a doctor by anyone who feels unwell. They are the precautions that go with the class for a skin allergy. The note has the clothing and the washing with soap and water.

The heading of section 4. Under it, for the eyes: contact lenses are looked for and taken out, the eyes are flushed with water for 15 minutes or more, the upper and lower lids lifted from time to time, and medical attention is got at once. The first supplier's sheet for its solutions gives several minutes and no line on medical advice for the eyes; the note gives the 15 minutes and the doctor at once as what this lab goes by. For the skin the section has the clothing taken off and the skin flushed with mild soap and water. The form of this supplier prints the same line for the eyes on every sheet of its that was read; it is carried all the same, as first aid on a sheet for the thing on the bench. Section 8 says that safety glasses, goggles or a face shield, a laboratory coat or apron and gloves are to be worn, and that an eyewash and a safety shower are to be at hand.

Section 10, the label of its list: the salt reacts violently, it says, with alkali metals, diazonium salts, oxidants and three compounds of the halogens that it names, and may explode or take fire. It agrees with NOAA's record, which the note names for the reaction with oxidising agents. On this bench the oxidiser is the potassium bromate.

Read and not carried. Section 2, its third line. Section 11 tells of an underactive thyroid and of goitre among the signs of exposure, and of a set of complaints that come of swallowing iodides for a long time. Why: the note has the thyroid from the third supplier's sheet, which gives it a hazard class; this sheet gives it none.

Why: the same line is on every sheet of this supplier that was read, for this lab and for the four before it, whatever the substance. This sheet gives the solution no class for the environment, and its section 14 answers No beside the words Reportable Quantity.

Why: the capitals name no hazard class, section 2 has none, and the form of this supplier prints the same call on every sheet of its that was read; the note is held to a length and gives the first aid for the eyes.

supports.where: The product named at the head of the sheet, whose number is SDS No. PP0398. The sheet carries the names of two suppliers of one company, Ward's Science and Boreal Science, and has English pages and then French ones; the English pages were read. It was read as the PDF served at the address above, which is one the supplier's own product page leads to: the page's link for safety data sheets opens the site's lookup of sheets by catalogue number, filled in with the product's own numbers, and this sheet is in the list it shows. The site's robots file closes its search by words to automated readers, and that search was not used; it does not close this lookup. The product page lists no option for sale on the day it was read; its list of sheets gave three addresses for this catalogue number. Two were opened: the one read is the later revision, and the other, of April 16, 2018, classes the solution the same way. The third was not opened. It is a sheet for a solution of the strength on the bench. Section 3 gives potassium bromate at 0.476% and water at 99.524%. 0.04 mol/L of potassium bromate is 6.68 g in a litre, about 0.67% (worked out, not read from a source), and 0.476% is what 0.04 mol/L comes to with a formula weight of 119, which is potassium bromide's; the supplier's list of sheets describes this product as potassium bromide too, with that weight. The name on the sheet, its CAS number 7758-01-2 and every hazard on it are potassium bromate's, and it is read as a sheet for the bromate; the percentage is taken for a slip.
At the foot of the last English page, after the words Revision Date; the sheet says that it takes the place of one of November 2, 2022. This is the revision the address served on the day it was read.
Section 2, its first line, the word in capitals, as on the first supplier's two sheets. The pictograms are the skull and the health hazard, GHS06 and GHS08.

Section 2, the first of the two hazard statements. The class printed for it is acute toxicity by breathing in, category 3, which does not fit the statement or its code: the statement, the code, the first-aid line and the precautionary statement P301+P310+P330 are all for swallowing, and the class is taken for a slip of the sheet's. The first supplier's sheet for its solution has the milder H303; this sheet, for a solution of the strength on the bench, keeps the H301 of the solid. The note says so, and goes by it; the statement itself is on the tile.

Section 2, the second of the two hazard statements; the class is for carcinogens, category 1B. Section 11 gives the listing of one agency, in its group 2B, as possibly carcinogenic to people, and a warning under a law of California. It agrees with the first supplier's two sheets, from which the tile and the note have the statement. Section 2 prints P201 and P202 too, on instructions got and read before use.

Section 4, the first of its lines. After the capitals: a doctor or a poison centre is called at once, and vomiting is brought on only if medical staff say so. The precautionary statement P301+P310+P330 of section 2 asks the same call at once, and the rinsing of the mouth. The first supplier's sheet for its solution asks for the call only if the person feels unwell; the note gives the call at once, after any contact and so after swallowing, as what this lab goes by, and says nothing of vomiting.

The heading of section 4. Under it, for the eyes: contact lenses are looked for and taken out, the eyes are flushed with water for 15 minutes or more, the upper and lower lids lifted from time to time, and medical attention is got at once. The first supplier's sheet for its solution gives several minutes, and medical advice only if irritation lasts; the note gives the 15 minutes and the doctor at once as what this lab goes by. The form of this supplier prints the same line for the eyes on every sheet of its that was read; it is carried all the same, as first aid on a sheet for the thing on the bench. Section 8 says that safety glasses, goggles or a face shield, a laboratory coat or apron and gloves are to be worn, and that an eyewash and a safety shower are to be at hand.
